title: Visualization Quality and Accessibility
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of visualization quality and accessibility and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply choosing accessible color palettes in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Visualization Quality and Accessibility is part of Data Visualization and Graphics. Start with choosing accessible color palettes and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: A truthful visualization needs labels, readable scale, contrast, context and a non-color-only signal.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: A truthful visualization needs labels, readable scale, contrast, context and a non-color-only signal. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.text: Compare choosing accessible color palettes using concrete trade-offs, assumptions and maintenance needs; state when each choice is appropriate.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Add descriptive axis labels and explain one limitation of the chart you choose. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Visualization Quality and Accessibility
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 128: Visualization Quality and Accessibility
plot(c(4, 5, 6), c(2, 5, 4), type = "b", xlab = "Observation", ylab = "Measure")

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For visualization quality and accessibility, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
